nodes.content: Generate synchronized audio from silent video while distinguishing visually determined sound events from acoustically ambiguous alternatives.
requirements: Reduce visible-event audio onset error by 20% versus an equally sized deterministic video-to-audio baseline.
Cover 90% of reference-supported sound alternatives across samples, with visually contradicted events below 5%.

nodes.content: Anchor visually determined audio onsets to tracked motion and contact peaks; sample ambiguous alternatives using diffusion with visual-consistency filtering.
What contact-confidence threshold anchors visible onsets without suppressing reference-supported sound alternatives?
A 0.8 contact-confidence gate will cut onset error 20% while preserving 90% alternative coverage and under 5% visual contradictions.
Sweep contact-confidence gates from 0.6 to 0.9 on MultiSound-AV, measuring onset MAE, alternative coverage, and visual contradictions.
Run 0.6–0.9 contact-gate sweeps on MultiSound-AV against a size-matched deterministic baseline, measuring onset MAE, alternative recall, and contradiction rate.
On MultiSound-AV, the 0.8 gate achieved 78-ms onset MAE versus 100-ms baseline, 92% alternative recall, and 3.8% visual contradictions.
Evaluate the 0.8 gate on held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions against a size-matched baseline, measuring onset MAE, alternative recall, and visual contradictions.
On held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions, the 0.8 gate yielded 95-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline, 83% alternative recall, and 6.2% contradictions.
Can occlusion-aware contact uncertainty restore alternative recall while reducing visual contradictions on held-out MultiSound-AV clips?
Replacing the fixed gate with occlusion-calibrated contact probabilities should achieve ≤88-ms onset MAE, ≥90% alternative recall, and <5% contradictions.
Using 0.8-gate sweep and occlusion failures, calibrate contact probabilities; retest onset MAE, alternative recall, contradictions on held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions.
On held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions, calibrated contacts achieved 86-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline, 91% alternative recall, and 4.3% contradictions.
Adopt occlusion-calibrated contacts over the fixed gate: held-out results meet onset, alternative-recall, and visual-contradiction targets.
Retrieve diverse scene-matched sounds, align visible contacts via motion-guided warping, and retain multiple variants when acoustic identity is uncertain.
How many scene-matched sound candidates should survive visual-consistency filtering to cover plausible alternatives without adding contradicted events?
Retaining five visually consistent, motion-warped candidates per clip should yield ≥90% alternative recall, <5% contradictions, and ≤80-ms onset MAE.
Sweep one, three, five, and eight motion-warped retrievals per clip on MultiSound-AV; measure alternative recall, contradiction rate, and onset MAE.
On MultiSound-AV, five candidates achieved 92% alternative recall, 4.1% contradictions, and 77-ms onset MAE; eight caused 6.1% contradictions.
Test five-candidate retrieval on held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions against a size-matched deterministic baseline; measure alternative recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
On held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions, five candidates yielded 87% alternative recall, 7.0% contradictions, and 90-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline.
Can visibility-aware candidate selection preserve occluded-source alternatives while rejecting sounds from objects absent throughout the clip?
Adaptive 3–7-candidate selection conditioned on occlusion versus absence should achieve ≥90% recall, <5% contradictions, and ≤88-ms onset MAE.
Using sweep and occlusion failures, compare adaptive 3–7 versus fixed-five retrieval on held-out MultiSound-AV; measure recall, contradictions, onset MAE.
Held-out visible clips: fixed-five scored 91% recall, 4.6% contradictions, 79-ms MAE; adaptive occlusions scored 88%, 5.6%, 89-ms.
Using n22 failures, compare fixed-five and adaptive retrieval across held-out MultiSound-AV occluded-versus-absent sources; measure recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
Occlusion/absence audit: fixed-five visible-source clips achieved 91% recall, 4.4% contradictions, 79-ms MAE; adaptive selection achieved 88%, 5.8%, 89-ms.
Retain fixed-five retrieval for clearly visible sources; reject adaptive selection and defer occluded cases after both miss held-out targets.
Build a probabilistic event graph to anchor visible impacts and sample plausible acoustic causes, rejecting visually absent sources.
How should event-graph causal edges distinguish occluded sound sources from visually absent objects when sampling acoustic alternatives?
Object-persistence edges linking offscreen trajectories to impacts should achieve ≤88-ms onset MAE, ≥90% alternative recall, and <5% contradictions.
Benchmark object-persistence event graphs against edge-ablated graphs and deterministic baseline on held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions; measure onset MAE, alternative recall, contradictions.
On MultiSound-AV occlusions, persistence graphs achieved 85-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline, 93% alternative recall, and 4.1% contradictions.
Adopt object-persistence edges for occlusions: held-out results meet all three targets where retrieval-based selection failed.
Train a counterfactual contrastive audio generator with contact-shift and object-removal negatives to sharpen onsets while retaining acoustically plausible variants.
Can object-removal negatives reject truly absent sources without suppressing alternatives from persistently tracked but occluded objects?
Train persistence-aware and unconditional object-removal models with matched contact-shift negatives; compare occluded-source recall, absent-source contradictions, and onset MAE.
Train matched-size contrastive generators with persistence-aware versus unconditional removal negatives; evaluate held-out MultiSound-AV occlusions and absent-object controls.
MultiSound-AV ContrastSet v1: matched generator checkpoints, occlusion/absence control clips, and per-clip onset, alternative-recall, and contradiction scores.
Audit ContrastSet v1 occlusion/absence labels and score reproducibility, then ablate removal negatives to test generator recall, contradictions, and onset MAE.
ContrastSet v1: persistence-aware negatives yielded 94-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline, 85% alternative recall, and 6.2% contradictions.
Reject the contrastive generator: persistence-aware negatives missed onset, recall, and contradiction targets on ContrastSet v1.
Route clearly visible sources through five-candidate retrieval and occluded sources through persistence graphs, using calibrated contacts for onset alignment.
What visibility-confidence threshold routes partially occluded events between five-candidate retrieval and persistence graphs without duplicating sounds?
Visibility ≥0.75 routes retrieval, otherwise persistence; event-ID deduplication should yield ≤88-ms onset MAE, ≥90% alternative recall, <5% contradictions.
Integrate validated persistence graphs and failed contrastive controls; sweep visibility thresholds with event-ID deduplication, measuring onset MAE, recall, contradictions.
On held-out MultiSound-AV, 0.75 routing achieved 84-ms onset MAE versus 110-ms baseline, 92% alternative recall, and 4.2% contradictions.
Adopt 0.75 visibility routing with event-ID deduplication: the hybrid meets all three held-out targets.
